clue.text: Agent having lunch and belching?

definitions.note: verb sense: food that comes back up is said to repeat on you

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
having lunch means eating

explanation.surface: A salesman burps his way through a lunch meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: when food 'repeats' on you, you burp it back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that repeats on a diner brings up wind, so the burping eater is literally doing this.

clue.text: With plenty of space, setter's chasing marsupial

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the setter's piece follows the animal

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a pouched mammal
the setter refers to themselves, so setter's means my

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker runs after a kangaroo across wide open country.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy describes somewhere spacious, with lots of room to move about.

clue.text: Rigorists would see opposition leader in underwear

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the underwear

parts.note: pants are underpants
Ed Miliband led the UK Labour opposition when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Sticklers would spot the opposition leader in his underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposition leader' tempts you to take O, the first letter of opposition; it is ED, for Ed Miliband, Leader of the Opposition in 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants insist on strict adherence to rules and detail, which is what rigorists do.

clue.text: Abolish article from almanac?

indicators.note: an article taken from the yearbook means one letter of it is removed

parts.note: an annual is a yearly publication such as an almanac
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Should we cut an entry from the yearly reference book?
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an A from ANNUAL; the question mark admits the almanac is only an example of an annual.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void or cancel, as a marriage or a law is abolished.

clue.text: Shove can make me stupid, almost

indicators.note: can make says these letters can be made into something else by rearranging
almost means the last letter of stupid is dropped

explanation.surface: Pushing someone around can make me look a fool, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts STUPID to STUPI; with ME those letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or push that sets something moving.

clue.text: It's fascinating about African currency, not missing a trick

indicators.note: about means the alluring word goes round the money

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous, alluring or fascinating
the rand is South Africa's currency, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Something alluring about money from South Africa, with no opportunity missed.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a GRAND SLAM means winning every trick in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a grand slam takes all thirteen tricks, so the winners lose none.

clue.text: Teaching must include every single one

indicators.note: the word Teaching must include, that is hold within it, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A teacher insists that every pupil must be covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Each refers to every individual member of a group, taken one at a time.

clue.text: Harassed medic needs space to cope with it

definitions.text: Harassed medic needs space to cope with it

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

indicators.note: harassed means troubled and harried, so the letters of medic are agitated

explanation.surface: An overworked doctor needs room to deal with a local disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an endemic illness is what an overstretched doctor must cope with.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic is a disease habitually present in a particular region, which local doctors must manage.

clue.text: It's obvious an establishment needs to get rid of rubbish

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for the noun, the act of doing this

parts.note: clear means obvious
taken as written
the Church of England is the established church, abbreviated CE

explanation.surface: Plainly a business must clear away its waste.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is the state church in England, hence 'establishment' for CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearance is the removal of unwanted stuff, as in a house clearance.

clue.text: Doc's plan may need revising when this comes

definitions.text: Doc's plan may need revising when this comes

indicators.note: revising a plan means reworking it, so these letters are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's schedule gets upset when the weather suddenly turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a sudden spell of freezing weather brings a rush of patients that wrecks a GP's plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief spell of sudden freezing weather fills surgeries and would upset any practice's schedule.

clue.text: Badger brew, or something stronger?

indicators.note: to brew is to mix ingredients up, so the letters of Badger are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Fancy a pint of Badger ale, or would you prefer something stronger?
explanation.walkthrough: Badger is a well-known English beer brand, which makes 'brew' look like a noun. ARDBEG is a malt whisky distilled on the Scottish island of Islay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Islay single malt whisky is stronger in alcohol than a bitter beer.

clue.text: From high to low, many contrived to sing with it

definitions.text: From high to low, many contrived to sing with it

indicators.note: contrived means devised artificially, so the letters of many are reworked

explanation.surface: A whole congregation, top voices to bass, managed to sing along with the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' turns MANY into YMNA, framed by H and L; the whole clue also describes a book a congregation sings from.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a hymn book, the volume a congregation holds while singing in church.

clue.text: Where the sea ends it turns to nameless EU country

indicators.note: turns means the little word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nameless means losing N, the usual abbreviation for name

parts.note: Denmark is a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: At the shoreline the tide turns, heading for a Scandinavian member of the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes TI from IT; DENMARK without the N for name gives DEMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left on a beach at the highest point the water reached.

clue.text: Bark at idiot in US intelligence

indicators.note: in places the fool inside the American agency

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the United States
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a fool working for American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' looks like a verb (to shout) but is the noun, a tree's outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is an aromatic tree bark, a coarser relative of cinnamon used as a spice.

clue.text: St Michael worked to make gold from lesser material

definitions.text: St Michael worked to make gold from lesser material

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters of St Michael are reshaped

explanation.surface: A saint toils to turn base metal into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged saint's name gives the person who tried to turn base metals into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist was a medieval practitioner trying to transmute base metals into gold.

clue.text: Appetiser hostile to old flame?

parts.note: anti means opposed to
a past love, with love as O, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A starter that turns against a former sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old flame' means a past love: PAST plus O, since love is nil (O) in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cured meats and vegetables served before pasta.

clue.text: Stupid shape said to be due to its implant?

definitions.text: Stupid shape said to be due to its implant?

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is spoken and the sound gives the written word

parts.note: stupid means silly and a cone is a shape

explanation.surface: Someone jokes that an odd-looking figure results from cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the whole clue as a description: an absurd figure caused by a cosmetic breast implant of this material.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone gel is the synthetic material used in cosmetic breast implants.

clue.text: 99 actors composed a sort of verse

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of actors are arranged anew

parts.note: IC is a crossword's Roman numeral for 99, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: Ninety-nine performers wrote a poem together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns ACTORS into ACROST. IC for 99 is not standard Roman usage (XCIX) but a crossword convention: I before C.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a poem whose line initials spell out a word or message.

clue.text: One might be discovered by Samoan river craft

definitions.text: One might be discovered by Samoan river craft

indicators.note: craft as a verb means to fashion skilfully, so these letters are refashioned

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Such a person might be found aboard a Pacific islander's boat on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like the noun for a boat, but signals the anagram; the whole clue describes a rower in that boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman is a rower, the person pulling the oars of a boat.

clue.text: Anglican name gets certain reproof

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A churchman's name draws a definite rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is formal strong disapproval, a rebuke or reprimand.

clue.text: Did it attract boys to Bunter?

definitions.text: Did it attract boys to Bunter?

parts.words: Did it attract boys to Bunter?
parts.note: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy, first appeared in a weekly boys' story paper of this name, and such a thing also attracts iron

explanation.surface: Was it what drew young readers to a famous fat schoolboy?
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a comic fat schoolboy from early twentieth-century British boys' fiction, first published in a weekly paper called The Magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the title of the boys' weekly featuring Bunter, and the word means an object that attracts iron.

clue.text: Spirit's used by some English as a curative?

parts.note: gin is a spirit, and spirit's stands for gins with the s

explanation.surface: Some English people take a tot of alcohol as medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the root's healing reputation is a matter of belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng root is a traditional herbal remedy reputed to restore health.

clue.text: Ground includes parking for a reptile

indicators.note: includes means the land holds the parking letter inside it

parts.note: ground means land or terrain
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A piece of land with a car park set aside for a lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, and turtles are reptiles.

clue.text: A singer sung a single note

indicators.note: sung signals that the voice word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist sang just one note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a banknote, not a musical one: a TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note, which sounds like TENOR in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is colloquial British for a ten-pound banknote, one single note of money.

clue.text: At the call of duty one takes avoiding action …

indicators.note: a call is spoken, so the word for a levy is heard rather than read

parts.note: a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: Answering the summons of duty, a person dodges.
explanation.walkthrough: To tack is to sail a zigzag course, changing direction to avoid something.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that tacks changes course, zigzagging, a way of steering clear.

clue.text: … to practise extortion, to be precise

definitions.meaning: to demand money with menaces or force payment
accurate and correct in every detail

explanation.surface: Continuing on, taking money by threats, to be accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to demand payment forcibly; as an adjective it means accurate.

clue.text: Scientific test involving two of the humanities

parts.note: Lit is short for literature, one arts subject
Mus is short for music, a second arts subject

explanation.surface: An experiment that somehow requires a pair of arts subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: Lit and Mus are standard abbreviations for literature and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A litmus test uses dyed paper that turns red or blue to show acid or alkali.

clue.text: Statesman?

parts.note: read as States-man, the man who stands for the United States

explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as 'States man': the bearded figure in a top hat who personifies the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: This bearded figure in star-spangled clothes is the national personification of America.

clue.text: Knock out, turning crazy

indicators.note: turning means the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Being knocked out sends someone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or render senseless, as with a blow to the head.

clue.text: Mistake in superintendence

definitions.meaning: an error made by failing to notice something
supervision or watchful management of something

explanation.surface: An error in management.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unnoticed slip and the act of supervising, two opposite senses of watching.
